posts.title: Job's Regular Practice
posts.excerpt: Long before Job lost everything, he was just a dad who got up early to intercede for his kids. Not panic prayer. A rhythm.
posts.description: Long before the suffering, Job was just a dad getting up early to cover his kids in prayer. Not panic prayer. A regular practice.

posts.title: While He Was Still Speaking
posts.excerpt: One messenger has not even finished before another shows up with worse news. And then another. The first thing Job did was fall on his face in worship.
posts.description: The messengers came faster than Job could process. He grieved and worshipped at the same time. What is in you when the messengers keep coming?

posts.title: How Can a Good God…?
posts.excerpt: Sitting in ashes, having lost everything, Job answers the most-asked question in the world in one sentence.
posts.description: Sitting in ashes, Job answers the most asked question in the world in one sentence. If we trust God with the good, we have to trust Him with the hard.

posts.title: If Only There Was a Mediator…
posts.excerpt: He could not have pictured a manger or a cross. But he felt the gap so deeply that he cried out for someone who could bring God and man together.
posts.description: Job did not know His name, but he felt the gap so deeply that he cried out for a mediator. Thousands of years later, that prayer was answered.

posts.title: Job 28:28
posts.excerpt: We talk a lot about wisdom. We rarely talk about where it actually comes from.
posts.description: Real wisdom starts with fearing God, and real understanding comes from actually walking away from what He calls wrong.

posts.title: Job 33:10
posts.excerpt: We go through a hard season and we start to make it about us in a way that is not even true.
posts.description: When we are suffering, it is easy to frame God as the enemy. Elihu called Job on it, and the correction is worth hearing.

posts.title: Job 42:3
posts.excerpt: He was not being sarcastic. He is not defeated. He is humbled. He is finally in the right place.
posts.description: Job finally gets it — and his response teaches us what it looks like to stop demanding answers from God and start trusting Him instead.

posts.title: Job 42:17
posts.excerpt: Full does not mean happy every day. It does not mean easy. It means whole. Complete. Rounded out with everything a real life includes.
posts.description: The last verse of Job is almost too quiet for a book with so much drama. But that is exactly why it matters.

posts.title: Psalm 2:12
posts.excerpt: You bow to Him and find joy. Or you do not, and you get consumed by your own life.
posts.description: The whole verse boils down to a choice. Submit or not. Take refuge or not. There is no middle ground.

posts.title: Psalm 4:4
posts.excerpt: Sleep on it. And be quiet in the meantime. That is such practical wisdom. Especially the silent part.
posts.description: Anger controlling you is sin. But anger itself is not. There is a difference — and this verse tells you exactly what to do with it.

posts.title: Psalm 18:39
posts.excerpt: There have been seasons where I have had to be strong. Not because I found it in myself. Because God armed me with it.
posts.description: He does not throw you into a battle empty handed. He equips you — and the strength shows up when the battle does.

posts.title: Psalm 19:13
posts.excerpt: What are the deliberate sins I have made peace with? The ones I keep doing because I have talked myself into believing they do not really count.
posts.description: Deliberate sin is the kind you knew was wrong and did anyway. David asked God to keep him from that. So should we.

posts.title: Psalm 25:19-21
posts.excerpt: He does not fight back with words. He does not try to prove them wrong. He turns his face toward God and asks Him to handle it.
posts.description: When the hate online is loud and the accusations are flying, David shows us what to do. Not clapbacks. Not receipts. Integrity and honesty.

posts.title: Psalm 33:10
posts.excerpt: Panic assumes God is not in charge. Faith assumes He is. And when I remember that He frustrates the plans of the nations, I can breathe again.
posts.description: When the world feels like it is spinning out of control, this short verse is exactly what you need to hear.

posts.title: Psalm 40:5
posts.excerpt: He answers a prayer and we say thank you and get on with our day. He rescues us and we exhale and go back to normal. We forget. Not because we are ungrateful. Just because we are moving.
posts.description: Most of us have more of God's fingerprints on our life than we ever pause to name. David stopped and counted. So should we.

posts.title: Psalm 50:14 & 23
posts.excerpt: Everything in you wants to focus on what is going wrong. And in that moment, choosing thankfulness costs something. You are laying down your right to complain. That kind of thankfulness is worship.
posts.description: Thankfulness is only a sacrifice when it costs you something. The easy kind is not remarkable. The hard kind is worship.

posts.title: Psalm 56:4
posts.excerpt: They can hurt me. They can lie about me. They can walk away. They can make my life difficult in a thousand ways. But they cannot touch the part of me that belongs to God.
posts.description: David knew exactly what mortals could do to him. He had been chased, betrayed, and hunted. And he still asked the question.

posts.title: Psalm 59:12
posts.excerpt: Pride does not free people. It captures them. That is a very different picture than the one our culture is painting.
posts.description: The world says pride is what sets you free. God's Word says pride is what locks you up. David uses one word that tells you everything.

posts.title: Psalm 71:18
posts.excerpt: Everything you have walked through, every prayer God answered, every hard thing He carried you through — it was not just for you. It was so you would have something to hand to the ones coming next.
posts.description: David did not ask for a quiet retirement. He asked to be used. Do not abandon me now — I still have something to give.

posts.title: Psalm 73:28
posts.excerpt: Being close to God and being covered by God changes what comes out of our mouths. If we are truly close to Him, and truly sheltered by Him, we cannot help but talk about Him. It leaks out.
posts.description: How good it is to be near God. That is not a quiet observation. That is a burst of joy from someone who has actually experienced His presence.

posts.title: Psalm 119:140
posts.excerpt: The promises that carried Abraham are the same ones that carry me. The promises that steadied David are the same ones that steady me. The promises that gave Paul confidence in a prison cell are the same ones that give me confidence in my own life today.
posts.description: God's promises have been thoroughly tested. Not just promised. Tested. Weighed. Held up to the fire and pressure of real situations, real people, real history.

posts.title: Psalm 138:8
posts.excerpt: The reason God is going to work out His plans for my life is not tied to how well I am performing. It is tied to who He is. His faithful love endures forever. His involvement in my life is not conditional on me.
posts.description: God is intimately involved in the plans for my life. Not because I have earned it. Because His faithful love endures forever.

posts.title: Psalm 141:5
posts.excerpt: We say we want to grow, we say we want to be sharpened, we say we want to be more like Jesus. But when someone actually walks up and tells us something hard about ourselves, most of us get defensive. David does the opposite.
posts.description: David did not just tolerate correction from the godly. He invited it. He called it a kindness. A soothing medicine. Something he did not want to refuse.

posts.title: Proverbs 1:31
posts.excerpt: The very lifestyle that promised to set everyone free is producing a generation that cannot get out of bed without medication. That is not a coincidence. It is the exact fruit Proverbs described thousands of years ago.
posts.description: Wisdom has been calling. People have been ignoring her. Verse 31 is the natural consequence. They eat the bitter fruit of living their own way.

posts.title: Proverbs 11:24
posts.excerpt: The most generous people I know are also the most joyful, the most peaceful, the most alive. They give freely. And they always seem to have more, not less. Generosity multiplies. Stinginess shrinks.
posts.description: Give freely and become more wealthy. Be stingy and lose everything. One of those upside-down truths that only makes sense in God's economy.

posts.title: Proverbs 18:13
posts.excerpt: We post before we research. We repost before we read the article. We form strong opinions in about four seconds and then broadcast them to everyone we know. And Proverbs calls it what it is. Foolish.
posts.description: Spouting off before listening to the facts is both shameful and foolish. This reads like it was written for the exact culture we are living in.

posts.title: Proverbs 20:3
posts.excerpt: It takes strength to walk away. It takes real self control to not engage. Anyone can pop off. Anyone can throw punches back. That is not honor. That is just reaction.
posts.description: The world says the one who never backs down wins. Proverbs says the one who walks away has honor. Those are very different definitions of strength.

posts.title: Proverbs 30:4
posts.excerpt: We tend to think of Jesus as a New Testament reveal. But this verse says otherwise. The Son was always there. The Old Testament was slowly asking a question. Jesus was always the answer.
posts.description: This verse is in Proverbs. In the Old Testament. Hundreds of years before Jesus was born. And it is already asking about His Son.

posts.title: Ecclesiastes 7:18
posts.excerpt: Trying to be too good, in the sense of trying to earn God's love, is its own kind of trap. It looks holy on the outside. But underneath, it is prideful. It is exhausting. It is performative.
posts.description: Solomon warns against two extremes — not just the obvious one. The performative kind of goodness is its own trap, and it gets talked about a lot less.

posts.title: Isaiah 7:3
posts.excerpt: I did not know Isaiah had a son. That was the first thing that caught me. I have read Isaiah more than a few times, but I never really stopped to think about the fact that he was a dad.
posts.description: Isaiah had a son, and his name carried a promise. A reflection on names that speak hope out loud, even in heavy seasons.

posts.title: Isaiah 8:7
posts.excerpt: God's care can look small and quiet compared to what the world offers. But the world's power always comes with a price. What we think will save us often ends up overwhelming us.
posts.description: Judah rejected the gentle waters of Shiloah and got the flood of the Euphrates instead. A reflection on quiet trust, worldly power, and a river that is drying up in the news.

posts.title: Isaiah 8:11-12
posts.excerpt: We are consuming so much of the same content, watching the same shows, scrolling the same feeds, following the same voices, that our thinking has quietly conformed to the world around us without us even noticing.
posts.description: God warned Isaiah not to think like everyone else, not to call everything a conspiracy, and not to live in dread. A word that feels written for right now.

posts.title: I Have a Plan for the Whole Earth
posts.excerpt: We have almost skipped that part of who He is. God is loving and God is just. God is kind and God brings judgment. Both are true. Both are Him.
posts.description: God has a plan for the whole earth, and it includes judgment. We have edited Him down to the parts we like. But He is both love and justice.

posts.title: Tell Us Nice Things
posts.excerpt: Do not tell us what is right. Tell us what feels good. Do not tell us the truth. Tell us what we want to hear. Thousands of years ago, this was the posture of the people God was warning. And it is the posture of most of our culture today.
posts.description: Thousands of years ago, people told the prophets to stop telling the truth. Today we are doing the same thing. A real God tells the truth even when we do not want to hear it.

posts.title: Generosity Has to Be Planned
posts.excerpt: Generosity has to be planned. Otherwise it does not really happen. We can talk all day about wanting to be generous. But life keeps moving and the generous thing we said we would do never actually happens.
posts.description: Generous people plan to do what is generous. They do not wait for leftovers. They start with the giving and build their lives around it.

posts.title: His Discipline Is Good
posts.excerpt: We know it in our heads and we resist it with our lives. When conviction shows up, we do not want to hear it. When God is trying to redirect us, we drag our feet.
posts.description: God's discipline is not punishment. It leads to life and health. But we still resist it, and it costs us.

posts.title: Forget All That
posts.excerpt: Throughout the whole Old Testament, God keeps telling His people to remember. And then here in Isaiah, He says something almost the opposite. Forget all that. It is nothing compared to what I am going to do.
posts.description: God told His people to remember for centuries. Then He said forget all that. What I am about to do is bigger. And it was.

posts.title: Should I Bow Down to a Piece of Wood?
posts.excerpt: This passage is honestly a little funny when you actually picture it. God is basically saying, do you not realize you made the idol yourself? You took a block of wood. You burned half of it to cook your dinner. And then you carved the other half into a god.
posts.description: God spells out the absurdity of idolatry. You burned half the block for dinner and carved the other half into a god. We still do the same thing, just not with wood.

posts.title: Never Again
posts.excerpt: At first glance this verse can be confusing. Because we know God does get angry. We know He does bring judgment. So how can He say He will never be angry or punish His people again? The answer points straight to Jesus.
posts.description: God says He will never again be angry and punish His people. That sounds impossible until you look at the cross. Jesus took the flood in our place.

posts.title: Truth Is Gone
posts.excerpt: This passage sounds exactly like our culture today. Truth is gone. If you speak the truth in almost any public space right now, you will pay for it. Anyone who renounces evil is attacked. That is exactly where we are.
posts.description: Isaiah described our culture thousands of years ago. Truth is gone. Anyone who renounces evil is attacked. But God sees it, and He is not done.

posts.title: Here I Am, Here I Am
posts.excerpt: God is not the one who is far. He is not the one hiding. He is not the one refusing to be found. He is standing there saying, here I am, here I am, to a whole nation that will not even turn its head.
posts.description: God is not the one who is far. He is standing there saying here I am to a whole nation that will not even turn its head. The distance is not on His end.

posts.title: When He Called, They Did Not Answer
posts.excerpt: Reading Isaiah, you feel the two sides of God almost verse by verse. One moment He is inviting. The next moment He is warning. Both are Him. That is not a contradiction. It is who He is.
posts.description: God calls and calls. But there is a point where the ignoring itself becomes the judgment. Isaiah shows both sides of God almost verse by verse.

posts.title: Find One
posts.excerpt: This whole verse is God essentially saying, find one. Find one just and honest person in this whole city, and I will spare it. One. That is all He is asking for.
posts.description: God told Jeremiah to search Jerusalem for even one just and honest person, and He would spare the city. One faithful life carries more weight than we realize.
